notes.name: Dr. L. Nair
notes.text: keth must never be used upward. To an uncle or any elder it is an insult ('upstart'). Subtitles must not put it in a younger person's mouth toward an elder unless the scene wants the insult.

notes.name: Dr. L. Nair
notes.text: Confirm G-RESPECT-2: tense suffix first, then -ji. veluriji, never velujiri.

notes.name: Dr. L. Nair
notes.text: tamba is the household, the family as a unit. For the building use vasa.

notes.name: A. Rao
notes.text: Young speakers use keth jokingly with older cousins close in age. Context decides; it is not always an insult.

notes.name: A. Rao
notes.text: Loans such as bus and phone stay exactly as in English.

notes.name: F. Qadri
notes.text: In rural speech loans take a final -u: busu, phonu, citiyu. Urban speech keeps them unchanged.

notes.name: F. Qadri
notes.text: 'Let us ...' seems to be root + -na (konana 'let us eat'). I heard it in the interviews; not confirmed with a second speaker.
